body.html: Finland Resort Inn's main draw is that it's a small, quiet hotel on the outskirts of Samut Sakhon with easy parking. The hotel has around 20 rooms at 9/9 Moo 4, Bang Thorat, Mueang Samut Sakhon — not in the heart of the Mahachai market district, but about a 14-minute drive to CentralPlaza Mahachai. It suits drivers, anyone in the area for factory business, or an overnight stop without the bustle of the town centre.

What real reviews praise most is that the rooms and bathrooms are spacious, with convenient parking. Several guests say the rooms feel open and comfortable, and for a low-hundreds rate you get plenty of space. Rooms come with air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free bottled water and a private bathroom, with free Wi-Fi throughout and daily housekeeping. The styling is plain and functional rather than fancy, but overall it's clean enough for a hotel at this price.

Another thing that sets it apart from small guesthouses is the on-site riverside restaurant and 24-hour reception. Khwan Khao River restaurant sits within the grounds, open for lunch and dinner, serving Thai and general dishes — handy when you'd rather not drive out for food. There's room service and late check-in too, useful if you arrive off-schedule.
"Spacious room, big bathroom, clean, easy parking, and a restaurant on site. Good for a one-night stop driving through Samut Sakhon — the staff were fine too."

The thing to be honest about is that the review scores are still mixed, and some platforms have few reviews. On Trip.com it sits around 6 out of 10 from a small number of reviews, while Google overall is in the "Very good" band from over a hundred reviews, and TripAdvisor gives roughly 4 out of 5. Some reviews note that the blackout curtains don't fully close and facilities are fairly limited. A few also mention past issues with booking and refunds, and feel the rate can seem steep for the service at times — which is why we'd suggest booking through a platform with free cancellation first.

Another thing to know is that the location is suburban and not walkable. Bang Thorat is a fairly quiet area with no shops or restaurants to stroll to as you'd find in central Mahachai, so getting around is awkward without a car. The hotel therefore suits drivers wanting quiet and parking more than anyone wanting to be near food and sights. If you want a walkable spot near markets and restaurants, look at the central-Mahachai options in this series instead.

Overall, Finland Resort Inn is a small suburban hotel that suits drivers wanting a spacious room, easy parking and quiet outside the town centre, at a low-hundreds rate. Rates start around ฿600 for a Standard room and climb to roughly ฿700–1,000 for a Deluxe or on busy dates. If you can live with a car-dependent location, limited facilities and mixed review scores, it's a worthwhile overnight stop for travel through Samut Sakhon.

faqTitle: FAQ — Finland Resort Inn Samut Sakhon

faq.q: Where is Finland Resort Inn in Samut Sakhon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Finland Resort Inn is at 9/9 Moo 4, Bang Thorat, Mueang Samut Sakhon. It's a suburban location, about a 14-minute drive to CentralPlaza Mahachai, with Wat Nuamkanon around 2 km away. Central Mahachai and the railway station are roughly a 15-minute drive — best for anyone with their own car.

faq.q: How much does Finland Resort Inn cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿600/night for a Standard room. Options range from Standard and Standard A to Deluxe and a family/twin room. Larger rooms and busy dates climb to roughly ฿700–1,000 depending on season and room type — always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Finland Resort Inn like — are they spacious?
faq.a: Real reviews praise the rooms mainly for being spacious, with large bathrooms. It's a small hotel of around 20 rooms; rooms have air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free bottled water and a private bathroom. The styling is plain and functional, clean enough for the low-hundreds rate, though rooms are lightly stocked.

faq.q: Does Finland Resort Inn have parking and a restaurant?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking and an on-site riverside restaurant (Khwan Khao River), open for lunch and dinner. There's free Wi-Fi throughout, a 24-hour reception and room service. It suits drivers, since there's nowhere to walk to nearby.

faq.q: Who is Finland Resort Inn best for?
faq.a: It's best for drivers wanting a spacious room, easy parking and quiet outside the town centre at a low-hundreds rate. It suits an overnight stop while travelling through Samut Sakhon more than anyone wanting to be near food and sights or without their own car.

faq.q: What are the review scores for Finland Resort Inn like?
faq.a: Scores are still mixed across platforms. Trip.com gives around 6 out of 10 from a small number of reviews, while Google overall is in the "Very good" band from over a hundred reviews, and TripAdvisor is roughly 4 out of 5. Common gripes are blackout curtains that don't fully close and limited facilities — we'd suggest booking with free cancellation first.
